question.problem: Consider the plane curve ${x}^{2}y=xy+4.$ Find a tangent vector to that curve at the point $(2,2).$
question.worked_solution:
First, we bring all variables to one side:

$$
\begin{aligned}{x}^{2}y & =xy+4 \\ {x}^{2}y-xy & =4\end{aligned}
$$

If we set $f(x,y)={x}^{2}y-xy$, our curve can be viewed as the level curve $f(x,y)=4.$ 

A tangent vector to the level curve that passes through the point $(2,2)$ can be computed as follows:

$$
t(2,2)={f}_{y}(2,2)\,i-{f}_{x}(2,2)\,j
$$

So, we calculate $t(x,y)$ and evaluate it at $(2,2):$

$$
\begin{aligned}t(x,y) & =\frac{∂}{∂y}({x}^{2}y-xy)\,i-\frac{∂}{∂x}({x}^{2}y-xy)\,j \\  & =({x}^{2}-x)\,i-(2xy-y)\,j \\ t(2,2) & =({2}^{2}-2)\,i-(2(2)(2)-2)\,j \\  & =2\,i-6\,j\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, our tangent vector is $2\,i-6\,j.$
